notes: 174 server tests passed across 47 files; the additional long-interval backoff regression and the complete final 7-test source suite passed. Together with 67 UI tests and 1 CLI test, there are 243 unique tests.
Real Beads initializes dependency-linked tasks for Alice and Bob. Only ready work starts; native result files prove UID/HOME/cwd. Foreign reads/polls/results and revoked grants are denied.
Repeated polling and post-restart lost-reply recovery retain the same reservation and native run ID, with one native admission row. Beads issues remain open, as specified by this read-only adapter.

Initial Docker attempts exposed reuse of a permanently stopped supervisor ID and a recovery fixture writing through a readonly database descriptor. The reader now persists a fresh ID after cleanup; the fixture uses the existing private recovery executable.

Final additive source/user/project adapter context was checked by the generic-adapter test and typecheck, then rebuilt into the final image; Beads ignores these metadata fields and its deployed execution path is unchanged.
Desktop and 390px mobile Task sources screenshots were inspected. Chrome checked saved history and disabled polling controls for a paused source.
Executed on Linux arm64 in Docker. The amd64 release checksum is pinned but amd64 was not executed in this run.

limitations: Only the Beads adapter is exposed; remote source configuration and encrypted per-user credentials remain in the plan.
Beads uses a complete bounded ready snapshot: at most 1000 tasks / 1 MiB; oversized responses fail without advancing checkpoint.
One immutable source per project/kind and one admission per task ID. Edits or reopening do not automatically create a new run.
No automatic Beads claim/close/sync, distributed consumer lock, multi-process scheduler lease or exactly-once external-effect guarantee.
Verified with stock Qwen and deterministic model, not corporate-fork authorization.
